title: Suppress Q256 uniformly with a cyclic fixed three-shear word
statement: For F3={(e1,e2),(e2,e3),(e3,e1)}, every input k and output k prime in Q256 have exactly one intermediate Fourier path: (k1 prime,k2,k3), then (k1 prime,k2 prime,k3). Its nominal couplings are k2,k3,k1 prime. Every nonzero matrix element has at least one nonzero integer coupling; calibration changes it by at most sqrt(3)/4<7/16, so the actual magnitude remains>1/2. Transverse sector size is<512. The accepted uniform Jacobi bound and L2-unitarity give a Schur bound over fewer than513^3 modes. For every rational0<zeta<=1/2, s=ceil[(2^1010*513^11/zeta)^3] gives sup_calibration ||Q256 U3(s)U2(s)U1(s)Q256||2to2<=zeta, with log s=O(1+log zeta^-1). This is arbitrary-accuracy fixed-block evacuation, not growing-cutoff or full critical-norm contraction.
